title: Christ will gather his elect, and Adam’s fall makes choice real
setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, a few days before the 26 September conference. Six elders and three other members were present. Revelation Book 1 says they differed over Adam’s transgression and asked the Lord about it. Many members were also eager about the Book of Mormon’s promise of a gathering in America. Hiram Page’s competing revelations about Zion were circulating at the same time.
summary: The revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, who will gather his people “as a hen gathereth her chickens”. It forgives the elders and calls them to gather the elect to one place on this land. It describes Christ’s coming in glory, the Twelve judging Israel, and the rising of the righteous dead. Signs, plagues, and the fall of the great and abominable church come first. After the thousand years, a new heaven and earth replace the old. The text then says all of God’s commandments are spiritual, not temporal. It explains the devil’s rebellion, Adam’s fall, and the time of probation given for repentance. It says little children are redeemed through Christ and cannot sin until they become accountable.

contextNote.title: Why temptation is allowed
contextNote.text: The elders had disagreed about Adam’s transgression. Verse 39 answers why the devil is allowed to tempt at all. Without temptation, people “could not be agents unto themselves”. The verse adds a plain image: without bitter, they “could not know the sweet”. Verse 40 then shows Adam tempted, yielding, and falling. Verse 42 holds back temporal death until angels can teach repentance and redemption. In this passage agency means a real choice, and the devil’s temptation supplies the other side of it.

ldsText: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Jesus Christ Will Gather His People” centers on this revelation’s promise of gathering. Verse 2 says Christ gathers those who hearken, humble themselves, and pray; which of those three most needs your attention now?
reviewNote: Read all 50 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, September 1830, with six elders present, a few days before the 26 September conference. JSP historical introduction read for the Revelation Book 1 heading (six elders and three members, disagreement over Adam’s transgression), the Book of Mormon gathering background, and the Hiram Page context. JSP notes September was inserted later; no exact day is known. Ezekiel and the Twelve are named but not added as people.
